critical_issues.msg: Hardcoded `--base master` will break if the repository's default branch is renamed to `main` or any other name.
critical_issues.suggestion: Use `--base ${{ github.ref_name }}` or read the default branch dynamically rather than hardcoding `master`.

critical_issues.msg: stdout_tail and stderr_tail are interpolated into a log format string using %r (repr) but may contain unescaped newlines, corrupting the workflow log structure.
stdout_tail and stderr_tail are interpolated into a log format string using %r (repr) but may contain unescaped newlines, corrupting the workflow log structure.

suggestions.msg: Silently swallowing errors with `2>/dev/null` on the first two pip install attempts hides real dependency resolution failures, allowing the job to proceed with an incomplete environment.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove `2>/dev/null` from all but the last fallback, or expose which step failed with `|| echo "fallback N failed"`.

suggestions.msg: The empty-diff guard only checks staged content; if Claude modifies a file then reverts it before the `git add -A` step, staged diff is non-empty and a spurious PR is opened.
suggestions.suggestion: Also run `git diff --quiet` (non-staged) alongside `git diff --cached --quiet` after `git add -A` to confirm actual changes beyond the plan commit.

suggestions.msg: `comment_and_label` labels first then comments, contradicting its own code comment which says 'Apply the skip-label BEFORE commenting'; if commenting fails after labeling succeeds the issue is left partially updated.
suggestions.suggestion: Rewrite so both API calls succeed or neither is attempted (at minimum call remove-label on comment failure), and update the comment to match the actual order.

suggestions.msg: If the process has already exited (`proc.poll() is not None`) and EOF arrives immediately, the loop continues without breaking and `open_fds` may never shrink, causing unnecessary extra iterations.
suggestions.suggestion: When `proc.poll() is not None`, break out of the loop directly instead of letting it fall through to the next iteration's empty-read path.

suggestions.msg: On Python <3.11, `max(1, timeout - elapsed)` can still produce a non-positive value due to float truncation edge cases; the comment claims the clamp is in the caller but it is not.
suggestions.suggestion: Add an explicit clamp: `remaining = max(0.1, timeout - (time.monotonic() - start))` and pass that to `proc.wait`.

suggestions.msg: `stream_claude` is called from `main` which already catches `OSError`, so the caller-side OSError catch on line 154 is redundant for the `proc.kill()` path but necessary for the `cmd` construction path; the error boundary is unclear.
suggestions.suggestion: Separate 'binary not found' (OSError at construction) from 'process timed out' (OSError at kill) into distinct return/exit paths for clearer error reporting.

suggestions.msg: json.JSONDecodeError is imported directly but `json` is also imported at the module level; the direct import is redundant since the exception class is already accessible via `json.JSONDecodeError`.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove `from json import JSONDecoder` and use `except json.JSONDecodeError` directly.

suggestions.msg: The `JSONDecoder` fallback loop in `extract_json` attempts raw_decode from every character onward until a dict is found — O(n²) in the worst case. Negligible in practice for small Claude output but is a latent inefficiency.
suggestions.suggestion: Slice `text = text[:8192]` before the loop to bound the worst case.

suggestions.msg: Retry logic (max_attempts) applies only to the Claude API call; transient network errors or rate-limit responses from GitHub during label/comment operations are silently skipped.
suggestions.suggestion: Wrap critical `run_gh` calls with a small retry loop (1–2 attempts, 2-second backoff) for HTTP 500/503/rate-limit responses.
